survey: A handheld calculator floats tilted against a yellow pi-pattern background, as an icon would. The rounded dark-blue body is one solid slab with soft bevelled edges. Near the top edge sits a red solar strip with four cells, set flush into the body. Below it is a grey display window, recessed into the face and evenly framed. The keypad is a 4x4 grid: three columns of blue keys and a right-hand column of four cyan operator keys. Every key is a separate raised cap on the face, with clear gaps between keys. The rows and columns follow the body's tilt and perspective. The keys are evenly spaced, none merge or overlap, and they all fit inside the body. The calculator has no stand or surface, which is normal for a floating item icon. Leaving out symbols on the keys and display is a simplification, not a construction fault.
